articles.title: Karma Is Not a Revenge Service
articles.titleHinglish: Karma Koi Badla Lene Wali Service Nahi Hai
articles.content:
Most modern uses of the word karma are about someone else. He cheated me, karma will handle him. She will get what she deserves. Used this way it is simply revenge with a spiritual accent — a way of outsourcing anger to the universe and waiting for a result.

The original idea is both less satisfying and far more useful. Karma means action. The teaching is about cause and effect operating on the one who acts, not a cosmic court that punishes your enemies on a schedule you find acceptable.

The part that is directly verifiable, without any metaphysics at all, is this: your actions shape you. A person who lies frequently becomes someone who assumes others lie. A person who takes what is not theirs lives with a low, permanent vigilance. A person who is cruel to people below them becomes someone whose warmth is conditional and who is nervous around anyone with power. None of that requires a ledger in the sky. Every action leaves a residue in the actor, and the residue is the mechanism.

The same holds in the other direction. Honesty repeated makes a person less afraid, because there is less to manage. Generosity repeated makes the world look less scarce. You do not have to believe in rebirth to notice that behaviour builds the character that then experiences everything else.

This reframing has practical consequences.

It stops the waiting. People spend years watching for evidence that someone who wronged them is suffering. That watch is unpaid work for a company that does not employ you, and it keeps the injury current. The only account you can affect is your own.

It removes the excuse for cruelty. Karma is frequently used to justify ignoring people who suffer — they must have done something. That is a cruelty dressed as philosophy, and it fails on its own terms, because your response to someone's suffering is itself an action with its own effect on you.

And it shifts the question from what will happen to them to what am I building. The action you take today is not a deposit toward a future reward. It is a small edit to the person who will take tomorrow's action.

One more honest point. This does not explain suffering, and any teacher who uses karma to tell a grieving person they earned it is misusing the idea. Bad things happen to careful, kind people constantly. The teaching was never a complete explanation of the world's unfairness; it was a statement about what your own actions do to you, and that part holds up.
articles.contentHinglish:
Aaj kal karma shabd ka zyadatar istemaal kisi aur ke baare mein hota hai. Usne mujhe dhokha diya, karma dekh lega. Use uska mil jaayega. Is tarah istemaal karo to yeh bas aadhyatmik lehje wala badla hai — gusse ko brahmand ko outsource karke nateeje ka intezaar.

Asli vichaar kam santosh dene wala aur kahin zyada kaam ka hai. Karma ka matlab hai karm — kriya. Shiksha yeh hai ki kaaran aur parinaam karne wale par kaam karte hain, na ki koi aasmani adaalat hai jo aapke dushmanon ko aapke manpasand schedule par sazaa deti hai.

Jo hissa bina kisi metaphysics ke seedha jaancha ja sakta hai wo yeh hai: aapke karm aapko banate hain. Jo baar baar jhooth bolta hai wo aisa insaan ban jaata hai jo maanta hai ki sab jhooth bolte hain. Jo doosron ka haq leta hai wo ek halki, permanent chaukanni haalat mein jeeta hai. Jo apne se neeche walon ke saath kathor hai wo aisa insaan ban jaata hai jiski garmjoshi shart wali hai aur jo taakat wale kisi bhi insaan ke saamne bechain rehta hai. Iske liye aasmaan mein khaate ki zaroorat nahi hai. Har karm karne wale mein apni chhap chhodta hai, aur wahi chhap poora mechanism hai.

Doosri taraf bhi yahi sach hai. Baar baar ki gayi imaandaari insaan ka dar kam karti hai, kyunki sambhaalne ko kam bachta hai. Baar baar ki gayi dariyadili duniya ko kam tangdil dikhati hai. Punarjanm maane bina bhi aap dekh sakte ho ki behaviour wo charitra banata hai jo phir baaki sab kuch anubhav karta hai.

Is nazariye ke practical nateeje hain.

Intezaar khatam hota hai. Log saalon is saboot ki talaash mein rehte hain ki jisne bura kiya wo dukh mein hai. Wo nigrani ek aisi company ke liye bina tankhwah ka kaam hai jisne aapko rakha hi nahi, aur wo chot ko taaza bana kar rakhti hai. Jis khaate par aapka zor hai wo sirf aapka apna hai.

Kathorta ka bahana hat jaata hai. Karma ka istemaal aksar dukhi logon ko ignore karne ke liye hota hai — kuch kiya hoga tabhi. Yeh philosophy ke kapdon mein zulm hai, aur yeh apni hi shart par fail hota hai — kyunki kisi ke dukh par aapki pratikriya bhi ek karm hai jiska apna asar aap par padta hai.

Aur sawaal badal jaata hai — "unka kya hoga" se "main kya bana raha hoon". Aaj kiya gaya karm kisi bhavishya ke inaam ka deposit nahi hai. Wo us insaan mein ek chhota sudhaar hai jo kal ka karm karega.

Ek aur imaandaar baat. Yeh dukh ki vyakhya nahi karta, aur jo guru karma ka istemaal karke kisi gham mein doobe insaan ko yeh kehta hai ki usne kamaya hai — wo is vichaar ka galat istemaal kar raha hai. Sambhalne wale, achhe logon ke saath bura lagataar hota hai. Yeh shiksha kabhi duniya ki na-insaafi ki poori vyakhya thi hi nahi; yeh is baat ka bayaan tha ki aapke apne karm aapke saath kya karte hain — aur wo hissa aaj bhi tikta hai.

articles.title: If Everything Is Destined, Why Try?
articles.titleHinglish: Agar Sab Kuch Likha Hai To Koshish Kyun
articles.content:
This question stops many people early, and it usually arrives dressed as philosophy while functioning as an excuse.

Start with the practical observation. You do not actually live as though everything is fixed. You look before crossing the road. You revise for exams. Nobody applies fatalism to traffic. It is applied selectively, almost always to the areas where effort feels hardest or where failure would be humiliating.

The traditional answer is more precise than the popular version. What is given is the hand — the family you were born into, the body you have, the country, the language, the era, the events that arrive without your consent. What is yours is the play. Two people with almost identical circumstances produce very different lives, and the difference is in what they did with what they were handed.

The Gita's framing is the most usable: you have the right to the action, never to the fruits. This is not a recommendation to be indifferent. It is a description of where your power actually lies. You can control the preparation, the hours, the honesty of the effort. You cannot control the interviewer's mood, the market that year, whether someone better applied on the same day. Attaching your peace to the second category is what produces exhaustion, because you are trying to control something that was never yours.

What this looks like in practice.

Do the work fully, then release the result rather than the effort. Most people do the reverse — they slack on the work and then grip the outcome anxiously.

Judge yourself on what was in your hands. Did I prepare, did I show up, did I behave decently? Those are answerable. Did it work out is a different question with too many other authors.

And notice when destiny is being used as an anaesthetic. It was not in my fate is sometimes acceptance, and sometimes the most comfortable sentence available to someone who has not done the work. Only you know which one you are saying, and the difference matters more than any argument about free will.

The honest position, in the end, is that nobody knows how much is fixed. What we do know is that the belief you hold changes your behaviour, and behaviour is one of the few things whose effects can be observed. The practical rule that survives every version of the argument: act as though the effort matters, and hold the outcome loosely.
articles.contentHinglish:
Yeh sawaal bahut logon ko shuruaat mein hi rok deta hai, aur wo aksar philosophy ka libaas pehen kar aata hai jabki kaam bahane ka karta hai.

Pehle ek practical baat. Aap sach mein aise nahi jeete jaise sab kuch fix ho. Aap sadak paar karte waqt dekhte ho. Exam ke liye revise karte ho. Traffic par koi bhagyavaad laagu nahi karta. Wo chun kar lagaya jaata hai — lagbhag hamesha wahan jahan mehnat sabse mushkil lagti hai ya jahan fail hona sharminda karega.

Paramparik jawab lokpriya version se zyada saaf hai. Jo diya gaya hai wo patte hain — jis parivaar mein janm hua, jo sharir mila, desh, bhasha, daur, aur wo ghatnaayein jo bina aapki ijazat ke aati hain. Jo aapka hai wo khel hai. Lagbhag ek jaisi paristhitiyon wale do log bahut alag zindagiyan banate hain, aur farq ismein hai ki jo mila usse unhone kiya kya.

Gita ka framing sabse istemaal karne laayak hai: karm par adhikaar hai, phal par kabhi nahi. Yeh udaseen hone ki salaah nahi hai. Yeh is baat ka varnan hai ki aapki taakat hai kahan. Aap taiyari, ghante, aur mehnat ki imaandaari par zor rakh sakte ho. Aap interviewer ke mood par zor nahi rakh sakte, na us saal ke market par, na is par ki usi din koi behtar apply kar gaya. Apne chain ko doosri category se baandh dena hi thakan banata hai, kyunki aap us cheez ko control karne ki koshish kar rahe ho jo kabhi aapki thi hi nahi.

Yeh practically dikhta kaisa hai.

Kaam poora karo, phir nateeje ko chhod do — mehnat ko nahi. Zyadatar log ulta karte hain — kaam mein dheele padte hain aur nateeje ko ghabra kar pakad lete hain.

Khud ko us par aanko jo aapke haath mein tha. Kya maine taiyari ki, kya main pahuncha, kya maine sharafat se behave kiya? Inke jawab hain. "Kaam bana ya nahi" alag sawaal hai jiske bahut saare lekhak hain.

Aur dhyan do ki kismat kab behoshi ki dawa ki tarah istemaal ho rahi hai. "Mere bhagya mein nahi tha" kabhi sweekar hai aur kabhi us insaan ke liye sabse aaramdayak line jisne kaam kiya hi nahi. Aap hi jaante ho ki aap kaunsi bol rahe ho, aur yeh farq free will par kisi bhi bahas se zyada mayne rakhta hai.

Imaandaar sthiti ant mein yahi hai ki kisi ko nahi pata kitna fix hai. Jo pata hai wo yeh ki aapka vishwas aapka behaviour badalta hai, aur behaviour un ginne-chune cheezon mein se hai jinka asar dekha ja sakta hai. Jo practical niyam is bahas ke har version se bach jaata hai: aise kaam karo jaise mehnat mayne rakhti hai, aur nateeje ko dheela pakdo.
